criteria.text: The response concludes that the Seller Note's New York governing law and exclusive New York forum split enforcement of the Note from Buyer's Delaware-law set-off and indemnity rights under the SPA. It identifies the location as Seller Note §10, explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.
hints: laws of the State of New York

criteria.text: The response concludes that the Taxes representation is not a Fundamental Representation and so survives only 18 months after Closing, which is shorter than tax assessment periods and contrary to the letter of intent. It identifies the location as SPA §1.1 (Fundamental Representations) or §9.1, explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that, because the Disclosure Schedule describes the "Business" as beer brewing at the single 1180 Furnace Street brewery, Seller's non-compete does not cover hard seltzer, contract brewing, taprooms or brewing at other locations. It identifies the location as SPA §1.1/§6.6 or Disclosure Schedule §1.1(a), explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Disclosure Schedule limits recovery for the wastewater Specified Matter to the $2,400,000 Indemnity Escrow Fund, which is shared with general claims, undercutting the SPA's uncapped carve-out and leaving Buyer exposed on the estimated $3,100,000 pretreatment cost. It identifies the location as SPA §9.5(b) or Disclosure Schedule §9.2(d), explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.
hints: solely from the Indemnity Escrow Fund

criteria.text: The response concludes that Feldspar Hollow's change-of-control consent under the Contract Brewing Agreement (about 28% of volume) is triggered by the sale but omitted from the Required Consents, so it is neither a closing condition nor indemnifiable once disclosed. It identifies the location as SPA §1.1/§6.3/§7.2(d) or Disclosure Schedule §4.4/§4.7(b)(4), explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Seller Note can be assigned to any person, including a competitor, without Buyer's consent. It identifies the location as Seller Note §8, explains why this matters to Tinav, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Purchase Price is $48,000,000, made up of $40,000,000 cash plus the $8,000,000 Seller Note.
The response states that the Seller Note has a principal amount of $8,000,000.
The response is a memo to the supervising partner in which each issue sets out its location (document and section), why it matters for Tinav, and a recommended fix.
The response expressly flags which issue or issues need urgent attention.
The response claims that SPA §11.5 restricts assignment of the Seller Note.
The response claims that the Taxes representation is a Fundamental Representation that survives until the statute of limitations expires.
